title: Set 227

sentences.ko: 우리 상사가 내가 다른 데 알아보고 있는 걸 알게 됐는데, 화를 내기는커녕 남아 달라고 연봉을 더 주겠다는 거야. 그래서 지금 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠어. 그만두고 싶은 마음이 거의 굳었었는데, 돈이 훨씬 많거든.
sentences.text: So my boss found out I've been looking for other jobs, and instead of getting mad, she offered me more money to stay. And now I don't know what to do, because I was pretty sure I wanted out, but it's a lot more money.

alts.text: My boss caught me job hunting, and instead of getting mad she offered me a raise to stay. Now I'm stuck, since I was pretty sure I was done there, but it's way more money.

My manager discovered that I have been looking for other positions, and rather than becoming angry, she offered me a higher salary to stay. I am now unsure what to do, because I was fairly certain I wanted to leave, but it is considerably more money.

sentences.note: **instead of getting mad** 는 화를 내는 대신에라는 뜻으로, 예상과 다른 반응이 나왔을 때 씁니다. **I wanted out** 은 그만두고 빠져나가고 싶었다는 말을 짧게 하는 구어 표현입니다.

sentences.ko: 아, 병원 간 거? 별거 아니었어, 진짜. 애들 안고 다니다가 근육이 좀 놀란 것 같대. 그래서 몇 주 무리하지 말라는데, 뭐, 그게 되겠냐고.
sentences.text: Oh, the doctor thing? It was nothing, really. She said it's probably just a pulled muscle from carrying the kids around, so I'm supposed to take it easy for a couple of weeks, which, you know, good luck with that.

alts.text: The doctor? Nah, it was nothing. She thinks I probably just pulled a muscle lugging the kids around, so I'm supposed to take it easy for a couple weeks. Yeah, good luck with that.

Regarding the doctor's appointment, it was nothing serious. She said it is most likely a pulled muscle from carrying the children, so I am meant to rest for a couple of weeks, which I expect will be rather difficult.

sentences.note: **take it easy** 는 무리하지 않고 쉬엄쉬엄 한다는 뜻입니다. **good luck with that** 은 그게 되겠냐며 비꼬듯 말할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

sentences.ko: 내 폰 좀 잠깐 봐 줄래? 타자 치는데 화면이 자꾸 꺼져. 무슨 통화 중인 줄 아는 것처럼. 껐다 켜 보기도 했는데 이제 뭘 더 해 봐야 할지 모르겠어.
sentences.text: Can you look at my phone real quick? The screen keeps going black while I'm typing, like it thinks I'm on a call, and I already turned it off and on again, so I don't know what else to try.

alts.text: Got a sec to check my phone? The screen keeps blacking out when I type, like it thinks I'm on a call. I already restarted it, so I'm out of ideas.

Would you mind taking a quick look at my phone? The screen keeps turning black while I am typing, as though it believes I am on a call. I have already restarted it, and I am not sure what else to try.

sentences.note: **real quick** 은 잠깐만, 금방이라는 뜻의 구어입니다. **turned it off and on again** 은 껐다 켰다는 말로, 기계를 다시 켜 볼 때 흔히 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 진짜 나가려고 신발까지 신고 있었는데, 언니가 전화를 한 거야. 언니 어떤지 알잖아. 그래서 전화 끊고 나니까 거의 아홉 시고, 헬스장은 열 시에 닫으니까 그냥 안 갔어.
sentences.text: I was literally putting my shoes on to go, but then my sister called, and you know how she is, so by the time I got off the phone it was almost nine, and the gym closes at ten, so I just didn't bother.

alts.text: Had my shoes on and everything, then my sister called, and you know her, so by the time I hung up it was almost nine. Gym closes at ten, so I just skipped it.
I was putting on my shoes to leave when my sister called, and you know what she is like, so by the time the call ended it was nearly nine o'clock. Since the gym closes at ten, I decided not to go.

sentences.note: **you know how she is** 는 걔 어떤지 알잖아라는 뜻으로, 듣는 사람도 아는 성격을 말할 때 씁니다. **didn't bother** 는 귀찮거나 소용없어 보여서 굳이 안 했다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 운동 가려다 말게 된 핑계 대기

sentences.ko: 윗집 남자가 아침 여섯 시쯤부터 운동을 하는데, 꼭 우리 집 천장 위에다 아령을 떨어뜨리는 것 같은 소리가 나. 지난주에 쪽지를 남겼는데, 오히려 더 시끄러워졌어.
sentences.text: The guy upstairs started working out at like six in the morning, and it sounds like he's dropping the weights right on my ceiling. I left him a note last week, but if anything it's gotten louder.

alts.text: Guy upstairs works out at like six a.m. now, and it sounds like he's dropping weights right on my ceiling. Left him a note last week, but if anything it's louder now.

The man who lives above me has begun exercising at around six in the morning, and it sounds as though he is dropping weights directly onto my ceiling. I left him a note last week, but if anything, the noise has become louder.

sentences.note: **if anything** 은 오히려, 차라리 그 반대라는 뜻으로 기대와 반대로 됐을 때 씁니다. **at like six** 의 like 는 대략, 한 쯤이라는 뜻의 구어입니다.

reviewed: 1번 한국어 '나가고 싶은 게 거의 확실했는데'가 번역투라 '그만두고 싶은 마음이 거의 굳었었는데'로 고침
4번 formal의 'as you know what she is like'는 문법이 틀려 'you know what she is like, so'로 고침
5번 casual의 'Upstairs guy's started'는 소리내어 읽으면 어색해서 'The guy upstairs is working out at like six a.m. now'로 고침
5번 한국어 '천장에 대고 바로 아령을 떨어뜨리는 소리가 나'가 어색해 '천장 위에다 아령을 떨어뜨리는 것 같은 소리가 나'로 고침
